A research question comes before a technique. Start with the question and its
current bounded answer; open the card for supporting studies, limitations, and
next tests.

::: {.hub-question-list}
::: {.hub-question-card}
### [When do promising signals fail?](failure-conditions.qmd)

Which request types, evidence gaps, and operational constraints make a ranking
or reference method unreliable?

<div class="hub-card-answer"><strong>Current bounded answer</strong> Failures cluster around ambiguity, entity resolution, evidence custody, scope changes, and over-tuned fusion, but no complete predictor exists.</div>

<div class="hub-badges"><span class="hub-badge hub-status-open">Open</span><span class="hub-badge">Low confidence</span></div>
:::

::: {.hub-question-card}
### [Can candidate-side semantic evidence improve query-only retrieval?](candidate-evidence.qmd)

When choosing an LLM, does it help to consider what each candidate model is good
at, not only compare the request with past requests?

<div class="hub-card-answer"><strong>Current bounded answer</strong> Yes on development evidence, subject to the evidence limits on the question page.</div>

<div class="hub-badges"><span class="hub-badge hub-status-partial">Partially answered</span><span class="hub-badge">Moderate confidence</span></div>
:::

::: {.hub-question-card}
### [How far can query-only routing go?](query-only-routing.qmd)

Can a new request be routed well by comparing it with historical requests,
before using candidate responses?

<div class="hub-card-answer"><strong>Current bounded answer</strong> Dense query neighbors are a useful stable control, but candidate-side evidence improved development results.</div>

<div class="hub-badges"><span class="hub-badge hub-status-partial">Partially answered</span><span class="hub-badge">Moderate confidence</span></div>
:::

::: {.hub-question-card}
### [How reliable must a generated reference be?](reference-reliability.qmd)

When a generated answer guides candidate comparison, when is it trustworthy
enough and when should it be reviewed?

<div class="hub-card-answer"><strong>Current bounded answer</strong> Gemini was the strongest reviewed default, but difficult and ambiguous cases still need selective escalation.</div>

<div class="hub-badges"><span class="hub-badge hub-status-partial">Partially answered</span><span class="hub-badge">Moderate confidence</span></div>
:::

::: {.hub-question-card}
### [Can model responses provide useful ranking evidence?](response-evidence.qmd)

Does comparing a request or reference answer with candidate responses help
choose the best models?

<div class="hub-card-answer"><strong>Current bounded answer</strong> Direct lexical response retrieval underperformed; bounded refinement and reference-based paths have separate evidence.</div>

<div class="hub-badges"><span class="hub-badge hub-status-partial">Partially answered</span><span class="hub-badge">Low confidence</span></div>
:::
:::
